question: Use a ridge plot to compare the distribution of tumor mutational burden (TMB) across 10 cancer types.

files.eval_guideline: Ridge plot must show TMB density distributions for all 10 cancer types as stacked overlapping curves; axis labels, color scheme, and cancer type ordering may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename tmb_ridge_plot.png and PNG image format, matching the requested ridge plot of TMB distributions across 10 cancer types. The other candidate, answer.md, is a Markdown document rather than the plot image.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires a visual ridge plot showing TMB density distributions for all 10 cancer types as stacked overlapping curves, while allowing labels, colors, and ordering to vary. Semantic comparison evaluates these required visual features without requiring pixel-level agreement.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show stacked TMB density distributions for the same 10 cancer types in the same order: melanoma, lung adenocarcinoma, bladder, colorectal, head and neck, stomach, breast, pancreatic, ovarian, and prostate. Both convey the same principal pattern: melanoma has the highest and broadest TMB distribution, lung adenocarcinoma and bladder follow, and breast, pancreatic, ovarian, and prostate cancers have lower, more concentrated distributions. The horizontal axes express equivalent units of mutations per megabase. The candidate uses greater overlap and scales each ridge to its own peak, whereas the reference retains differing peak heights. Colors, label placement, and axis limits also differ, but these are acceptable under the evaluation guideline. The candidate adds sample sizes, median values and markers, a 10 mutations/Mb cutoff, and a Kruskal–Wallis result; these annotations cannot be verified from the reference alone. Small differences in density contours and tails prevent confirmation of identical underlying data, but no cancer types or essential distribution patterns are missing, and the candidate satisfies the requested ridge-plot comparison.
